requirements.text: The vehicle bumper shall be struck at 40 km/h with a legform that simulates the impact response of an adult's leg.
Vehicles with a lower bumper height of less than 425 mm shall be tested with a lower legform.
Vehicles with a lower bumper height of more than 500 mm shall be tested with an upper legform test device.
Vehicles with a lower bumper height between 425 mm and 500 mm shall be tested with either the lower legform or the upper legform, chosen by the manufacturer.
In the lower legform to bumper test, the vehicle shall meet limits on lateral knee bending angle, knee shearing displacement and lateral tibia acceleration.
In the upper legform to bumper test, the vehicle shall meet limits on the instantaneous sum of the impact forces with respect to time and on the bending moment.

The vehicle bumper shall meet minimum performance requirements for leg protection by subjecting pedestrians to lower impact forces when impacted by a legform impactor that simulates the leg of a mid-size adult male.
The vehicle bumper shall be evaluated by impact with either a lower legform impactor or an upper legform impactor, depending on the height of the bumper.
In the lower legform to bumper test, the maximum lateral knee bending angle shall be ≤ 19.0°.
In the lower legform to bumper test, the maximum lateral knee shearing displacement shall be ≤ 6.0 mm.
In the lower legform to bumper test, the maximum lateral tibia acceleration shall be ≤ 170g.
The bumper shall meet the maximum lateral tibia acceleration limit of 170g except within bumper test widths nominated by the manufacturer of up to 264 mm in total.
Within the manufacturer-nominated bumper test widths of up to 264 mm in total, the acceleration measured at the upper end of the tibia shall not exceed 250g.
Vehicles with a lower bumper height of more than 500 mm shall be subject to an upper legform test requiring the bumper to be energy absorbing.

For vehicles with a lower bumper height greater than, or equal to, 425 mm and less than 500 mm, either the lower legform to bumper requirements of paragraph 4.1.1. or the upper legform to bumper requirements of paragraph 4.1.2., at the choice of the manufacturer, shall be applied.
For vehicles with a lower bumper height of greater than, or equal to, 500 mm, the upper legform to bumper requirements of paragraph 4.1.2. shall be applied.

Compliance of the bumper with the lower legform to bumper performance requirements specified in paragraph 5.1.1. shall be verified using the test impactor specified in paragraph 6.3.1.1. and the test procedures specified in paragraph 7.1.1.

For vehicles with a lower bumper height greater than or equal to 425 mm and less than 500 mm where the upper legform to bumper test is applied, compliance with the performance requirements specified in paragraph 5.1.2. shall be verified using the test impactor specified in paragraph 6.3.1.2. and the test procedures specified in paragraph 7.1.2.
When tested in accordance with paragraph 7.1.1. (flexible lower legform to bumper), the absolute value of the maximum dynamic medial collateral ligament elongation at the knee shall not exceed 22 mm.
When tested in accordance with paragraph 7.1.1. (flexible lower legform to bumper), the maximum dynamic anterior cruciate ligament and posterior cruciate ligament elongation shall not exceed 13 mm.
When tested in accordance with paragraph 7.1.1. (flexible lower legform to bumper), the absolute value of dynamic bending moments at the tibia shall not exceed 340 Nm.

Where the manufacturer nominates bumper test widths up to a maximum of 264 mm in total, the absolute value of the tibia bending moment within those widths shall not exceed 380 Nm when tested in accordance with paragraph 7.1.1. (flexible lower legform to bumper).
When tested in accordance with paragraph 7.1.2. (upper legform to bumper), the instantaneous sum of the impact forces with respect to time shall not exceed 7.5 kN.
When tested in accordance with paragraph 7.1.2. (upper legform to bumper), the bending moment on the test impactor shall not exceed 510 Nm.
When the vehicle is tested as a DPPS (deployable pedestrian protection system) in headform tests, the test conditions and requirements in Annex 1 shall apply.
All devices designed to protect vulnerable road users when impacted by the vehicle shall be correctly activated before and/or be active during the relevant test.
The manufacturer shall show that any devices designed to protect vulnerable road users will act as intended in a pedestrian impact.

For vehicle components which could change shape or position, other than active devices to protect pedestrians, and which have more than one fixed shape or position, the vehicle shall comply with the components in each fixed shape or position.
When tested as a DPPS, the vehicle shall be adjusted as specified in the test procedure defined in Annex 1.
The bumper shall meet the flexible lower legform impactor to bumper test requirements at an impact velocity of the impactor when striking the bumper of 11.1 ± 0.2 m/s.
The impact velocity of the upper legform impactor when striking the bumper shall be 11.1 ± 0.2 m/s.
If all of the prerequisites are met, the vehicle fitted with a DPPS shall be tested with the DPPS activated as intended for the entire headform test area.
If any of the prerequisites from paragraphs 1.2 to 1.7 of Annex 1 are not met, the vehicle fitted with a DPPS shall be tested with the DPPS in the undeployed position.

For protection below the lower deployment threshold speed of the DPPS, the vehicle shall meet the headform test procedures specified in paragraphs 7.2 to 7.4 with the impact speed specified at 0.9 times the lower deployment threshold speed, where the allocation of the HIC1700 and HIC1000 Zones may differ from those at nominal velocity (9.7 m/s) headform impact tests according to paragraph 5.2.4.
In the headform test for protection below the lower deployment threshold speed of the DPPS, the HIC shall comply with paragraph 5.2.3. of the Regulation.
The lowest speed of activation (lower deployment velocity threshold) of the DPPS shall be specified by the vehicle manufacturer.

For the system deployment verification of the DPPS, sensor activation tests with the FlexPLI, as specified in paragraph 6.3.1.1. of this Regulation, shall be performed within the detection test area at the DPPS lower deployment velocity threshold.
For DPPS sensing system verification, a test with the FlexPLI shall be performed at nominal velocity (11.1m/s) at vehicle centreline (Y0).
The total response time (TRT) of the DPPS shall be confirmed by using the FlexPLI at the vehicle speed of 11.1 m/s and at the vehicle centreline (Y0).
The ESA sample(s) submitted for ESA type approval shall be clearly and indelibly marked with the manufacturer's trade name or mark and the type designation.

In case an ESA is (part of) a light source, the ESA shall either have an approval number granted according to Regulation No. 37, Regulation No. 99 or Regulation No. 128, or be shown by a test report from a Technical Service designated by the Type Approval Authority to be not mechanically interchangeable with any light source according to Regulation No. 37, Regulation No. 99 or Regulation No. 128.
ESAs which are intentional RF transmitters and which have not received type approval in conjunction with a vehicle manufacturer shall be supplied with suitable installation guidelines.

An approval mark as described in paragraph 5.3 shall be affixed to every ESA conforming to a type approved under UN Regulation No. 10, except that no marking is required for electrical/electronic systems built into vehicles which are approved as units.

A vehicle and its electrical/electronic system(s) or ESA(s) shall be designed, constructed and fitted in such a way as to enable the vehicle, in normal conditions of use, to comply with the requirements of UN Regulation No. 10.
ESA(s) shall be tested for radiated and conducted emissions and for immunity to radiated and conducted disturbances.

If measurements are made using the method described in Annex 7, the ESA broadband type approval limit shall be 62 to 52 dB microvolts/m in the 30 to 75 MHz frequency band, this limit decreasing logarithmically with frequencies above 30 MHz, as shown in Appendix 6.

If measurements are made using the method described in Annex 7, the ESA broadband type approval limit shall be 52 to 63 dB microvolts/m in the 75 to 400 MHz band, this limit increasing logarithmically with frequencies above 75 MHz, as shown in Appendix 6.
If measurements are made using the method described in Annex 7, the ESA broadband type approval limit shall remain constant at 63 dB microvolts/m in the 400 to 1,000 MHz frequency band.
On the ESA representative of its type, the measured broadband values, expressed in dB microvolts/m, shall be below the ESA broadband type approval limits.
The narrowband electromagnetic radiation generated by the ESA representative of its type shall be measured by the method described in Annex 8.

If measurements are made using the method described in Annex 8, the ESA narrowband type approval limit shall be 52 to 42 dB microvolts/m in the 30 to 75 MHz frequency band, this limit decreasing logarithmically with frequencies above 30 MHz, as shown in Appendix 7.

If measurements are made using the method described in Annex 8, the ESA narrowband type approval limit shall be 42 to 53 dB microvolts/m in the 75 to 400 MHz band, this limit increasing logarithmically with frequencies above 75 MHz, as shown in Appendix 7.
If measurements are made using the method described in Annex 8, the ESA narrowband type approval limit shall remain constant at 53 dB microvolts/m in the 400 to 1,000 MHz frequency band.
On the ESA representative of its type, the measured narrowband value, expressed in dB microvolts/m, shall be below the ESA narrowband type approval limits.

The emission of transient conducted disturbances on 12/24 V supply lines of the ESA representative of its type shall be tested by the method(s) according to ISO 7637-2 as described in Annex 10 for the levels given in Table 1.
The immunity to electromagnetic radiation of the ESA representative of its type shall be tested by the method(s) chosen from those described in Annex 9.

For the stripline method as described in Annex 9, the ESA representative of its type shall be immune at a test level of 60 V/m in the 20 to 400 MHz frequency range in over 90 per cent of the 20 to 6,000 MHz frequency band, and at a minimum test level of 50 V/m over the whole 20 to 400 MHz frequency range.

For the TEM cell method as described in Annex 9, the ESA representative of its type shall be immune at a test level of 75 V/m in the 20 to 200 MHz frequency range in over 90 per cent of the 20 to 6,000 MHz frequency band, and at a minimum test level of 62,5 V/m over the whole 20 to 200 MHz frequency range.

For the BCI method as described in Annex 9, the ESA representative of its type shall be immune at a test level of 60 mA in the 20 to 400 MHz frequency range in over 90 per cent of the 20 to 6,000 MHz frequency band, and at a minimum test level of 50 mA over the whole 20 to 400 MHz frequency range.

For the ALSE method as described in Annex 9, the ESA representative of its type shall be immune at a test level of 30 V/m in the 80 to 2,000 MHz frequency range in over 90 per cent of the 20 to 6,000 MHz frequency band, and at a minimum test level of 25 V/m over the whole 80 to 2,000 MHz frequency range.

For the ALSE method as described in Annex 9, the ESA representative of its type shall be immune at a test level of 10 V/m in the 2,000 to 6,000 MHz frequency range in over 90 per cent of the 20 to 6,000 MHz frequency band, and at a minimum test level of 8 V/m over the whole 2,000 to 6,000 MHz frequency range.

For the reverberation chamber method as described in Annex 9, the ESA representative of its type shall be immune at a test level of 21 V/m in the LUF to 2,000 MHz frequency range in over 90 per cent of the 20 to 6,000 MHz frequency band, and at a minimum test level of 18 V/m over the whole LUF to 2,000 MHz frequency range.

The ESA representative of its type shall show no degradation of performance of "immunity related functions" during the tests performed in accordance with Annex 9 in order to be considered as complying with immunity requirements.

The immunity of the ESA representative of its type to transient disturbances conducted along 12/24 V supply lines shall be tested by the method(s) according to ISO 16750-2 for starting profile and ISO 7637-2 for pulses 1, 2a, 2b, 3a and 3b, as described in Annex 10, with the test levels given in Tables 3a and 3b.

The ESA shall meet the functional status classification as defined in ISO 16750-1 for the starting profile and the Functional Performance Status Classification (FPSC) as in ISO 7637-1 for pulses 1, 2a, 2b, 3a and 3b.

For the starting profile test, which is only applicable to ESAs that could be installed in vehicles with internal combustion engines which are started with a 12V/24V starter motor, the ESA shall meet immunity test level II for 12 V and 24 V systems with 10 pulses, with functional status B for immunity related functions of ESA which shall be operational during engine start phases, functional status C for immunity related functions of other ESA, and functional status D for functions not related to immunity related functions.

For test pulse 1, the ESA shall meet immunity test level -75 V for 12 V systems and -450 V for 24 V systems with 500 pulses, with FPSC III for immunity related functions and FPSC III for functions not related to immunity related functions.

For test pulse 2a, the ESA shall meet immunity test level +37 V for 12 V systems and +37 V for 24 V systems with 500 pulses, with FPSC I for immunity related functions and FPSC III for functions not related to immunity related functions.

For test pulse 2b, the ESA shall meet immunity test level +10 V for 12 V systems and +20 V for 24 V systems with 10 pulses, with FPSC II for immunity related functions and FPSC III for functions not related to immunity related functions.

For test pulse 3a, the ESA shall meet immunity test level -112 V for 12 V systems and -150 V for 24 V systems for a test duration of 1 h, with FPSC I for immunity related functions and FPSC III for functions not related to immunity related functions.

For test pulse 3b, the ESA shall meet immunity test level +75 V for 12 V systems and +150 V for 24 V systems for a test duration of 1 h, with FPSC I for immunity related functions and FPSC III for functions not related to immunity related functions.

Where a vehicle or electrical/electronic system or ESA does not include an electronic oscillator with an operating frequency greater than 9 kHz, it shall be deemed to comply with paragraph 6.3.2. or 6.6.2. and with Annexes 5 and 8.
ESAs with no immunity related functions need not be tested for immunity to radiated disturbances and shall be deemed to comply with paragraph 6.8. and with Annex 9.

ESAs that are not switched, contain no switches or do not include inductive load need not be tested for emission of transient conducted disturbances on 12/24 V supply lines and shall be deemed to comply with paragraph 6.7.
RF transmitters shall be tested in the transmit mode.

Spurious emissions of RF transmitters shall be subject to the requirements of this Regulation, whereas wanted emissions (e.g. from RF transmitting systems) within the necessary bandwidth and out of band emissions are disregarded.

A vehicle and its electrical/electronic system(s) or ESA(s) shall be so designed, constructed and fitted as to enable the vehicle, in configuration "REESS charging mode coupled to the power grid", to comply with the requirements of this Regulation.

The vehicle shall comply with the radiated emission limits throughout the frequency range 30 to 1,000 MHz for measurements performed in an absorber lined shielded enclosure (ALSE) or an outdoor test site (OTS).
The vehicle shall meet the narrowband electromagnetic emission requirements when tested according to CISPR 12, if not otherwise stated in Annex 5.

The vehicle narrowband emission limits shall apply throughout the frequency range 30 to 1,000 MHz for measurements performed in an absorber lined shielded enclosure (ALSE) or an outdoor test site (OTS).

The vehicle electronic systems shall demonstrate immunity when the vehicle is subjected to electromagnetic fields according to ISO 11451-2 in an ALSE with front irradiation, for vehicles not considered as "large vehicles", at the test levels defined in paragraph 6.4.2.1. of the Regulation.

In the "50 km/h mode" vehicle immunity test, with the direction indicator on the driver's side ON, the direction indicator shall not exhibit a frequency change (lower than 0.75 Hz or greater than 2.25 Hz) or a duty cycle change (lower than 25 per cent or greater than 75 per cent).
In the "50 km/h mode" vehicle immunity test, with the alarm unset, the vehicle shall not exhibit an unexpected activation of the alarm.

In the "50 km/h mode" vehicle immunity test, with airbag and safety restraint systems operational with inhibited passenger airbag if this function exists, the vehicle shall not exhibit an unexpected activation.
The ESA under test for broadband electromagnetic emissions shall be in normal operation mode, preferably in maximum load.

The broadband radiated emission limits for the ESA shall apply throughout the frequency range 30 to 1,000 MHz for measurements performed in an absorber lined shielded enclosure (ALSE) or open area test site (OATS).
The ESA under test for narrowband electromagnetic emissions shall be in normal operation mode, preferably in maximum load.

The ESA radiated narrowband electromagnetic emissions shall comply with the limits throughout the frequency range 30 to 1,000 MHz for measurements performed in an absorber lined shielded enclosure (ALSE) or open area test site (OATS).

ESAs shall comply with the immunity requirements of any combination, at the manufacturer's discretion, of the absorber chamber test according to ISO 11452-2, TEM cell testing according to ISO 11452-3, bulk current injection testing according to ISO 11452-4, stripline testing according to ISO 11452-5 or reverberation chamber test according to ISO 11452-11, provided that the results cover the full frequency range specified in paragraph 3.1. of Annex 9, with frequency range and general test conditions based on ISO 11452-1.

ESAs in configuration "REESS charging mode coupled to the power grid" shall comply with the requirements of the combination of the absorber chamber test according to ISO 11452-2 and bulk current injection testing according to ISO 11452-4, at the manufacturer's discretion, provided that the results cover the full frequency range specified in paragraph 3.1. of Annex 9, with frequency range and general test conditions based on ISO 11452-1.
The ESA shall be tested under test conditions according to ISO 11452-1.
The ESA under test shall be switched on and stimulated to be in normal operation condition during the immunity tests.
The ESA immunity measurements shall be made in the 20 to 6,000 MHz frequency range with frequency steps according to ISO 11452-1.

The ESA immunity test signal modulation shall be AM (amplitude modulation), with 1 kHz modulation and 80 per cent modulation depth in the 20 to 400 MHz frequency range, if not otherwise agreed between Technical Service and ESA manufacturer.

The ESA immunity test signal modulation shall be PM2 (pulse modulation type 2), Ton 3 µs, period 3,333 µs in the 2,700 to 3,100 MHz frequency range, if not otherwise agreed between Technical Service and ESA manufacturer.

The ESA immunity test signal modulation shall be PM3 (pulse modulation type 3), Ton 500 µs, period 1,000 µs in the 380 to 2,700 MHz and the 3,100 to 6,000 MHz frequency ranges, if not otherwise agreed between Technical Service and ESA manufacturer.
The ESA shall be immune to conducted transients on the vehicle power supply.
The ESA shall limit conducted transients from the ESA to the vehicle power supply.

The ESA shall be immune to the test pulses 1, 2a, 2b, 3a and 3b according to ISO 7637-2 applied to the 12/24 V supply lines as well as to other connections of the ESA which may be operationally connected to supply lines.

The ESA shall be immune to the starting profile according to ISO 16750-2 applied to the 12/24 V supply lines as well as to other connections of the ESA which may be operationally connected to supply lines, except for ESAs that are exclusively reserved for mounting on electric vehicles (vehicles without 12V/24V starter motor).

The emission of transient conducted disturbances generated by the ESA on 12/24 V supply lines shall be measured according to ISO 7637-2 on the supply lines as well as on other connections of the ESA which may be operationally connected to supply lines.
For vehicles with a lower bumper height at the test position of less than 425 mm, the bumper shall meet the flexible lower legform to bumper requirements.

For vehicles with a lower bumper height at the test position greater than, or equal to, 425 mm and less than 500 mm, the bumper shall meet either the flexible lower legform to bumper requirements or the upper legform to bumper requirements, at the choice of the manufacturer.
For vehicles with a lower bumper height at the test position greater than, or equal to, 500 mm, the bumper shall meet the upper legform to bumper requirements.

When the bumper is tested with the flexible lower legform impactor in accordance with Annex 5, paragraph 1, the absolute value of the maximum dynamic medial collateral ligament elongation at the knee shall not exceed 22 mm.

When the bumper is tested with the flexible lower legform impactor in accordance with Annex 5, paragraph 1, the maximum dynamic anterior cruciate ligament and posterior cruciate ligament elongation shall not exceed 13 mm.
When the bumper is tested with the flexible lower legform impactor in accordance with Annex 5, paragraph 1, the absolute value of dynamic bending moments at the tibia shall not exceed 340 Nm.
Where the manufacturer nominates bumper test widths up to a maximum of 264 mm in total as a relaxation zone, the absolute value of the tibia bending moment in those widths shall not exceed 380 Nm.
When the bumper is tested with the upper legform impactor in accordance with Annex 5, paragraph 2, the instantaneous sum of the impact forces with respect to time shall not exceed 7.5 kN.
When the bumper is tested with the upper legform impactor in accordance with Annex 5, paragraph 2, the bending moment on the test impactor shall not exceed 510 Nm.

When tested with the child and adult headforms in accordance with Annex 5, paragraphs 3, 4 and 5, the HIC recorded shall not exceed 1,000 over two thirds of the combined bonnet top test area and the windscreen test area, measuring points in the cowl monitoring area not being taken into consideration.
When tested with the child and adult headforms in accordance with Annex 5, paragraphs 3, 4 and 5, the HIC recorded shall not exceed 1,000 over two-thirds of the bonnet top test area.
When tested with the child and adult headforms in accordance with Annex 5, paragraphs 3, 4 and 5, the HIC for the remaining test areas shall not exceed 1,700 for both headforms.
In case there is only a child headform test area, the HIC recorded shall not exceed 1,000 over two thirds of the test area.
In case there is only a child headform test area, the HIC for the remaining area shall not exceed 1,700.
When tested with the child headform in accordance with Annex 5, paragraphs 3 and 4, the HIC recorded shall not exceed 1,000 over a minimum of one half of the child headform test area.
When tested with the child headform in accordance with Annex 5, paragraphs 3 and 4, the HIC for the remaining areas shall not exceed 1,700.

In the case of a vehicle fitted with an ARHSS which could change the vehicle height at the front axle more than 20 mm from the nominal for any vehicle speed between 25 and 40 km/h, compliance with the biomechanical limits of the flexible lower legform to bumper and upper legform to bumper requirements respectively shall be demonstrated, with the agreement of the technical service, by a limited number of legform tests or by numerical simulation.
All devices designed to protect vulnerable road users when impacted by the vehicle shall be correctly activated before and/or be active during the relevant test.
The manufacturer shall show that any devices designed to protect vulnerable road users will act as intended in a pedestrian impact.

For vehicle components which could change shape or position, other than active devices to protect pedestrians, and which have more than one fixed shape or position, the vehicle shall comply with the pedestrian protection requirements with the components in each fixed shape or position.

The bumper shall meet the lower legform to bumper test requirements with the impact velocity vector in the horizontal plane and parallel to the longitudinal vertical plane of the vehicle, with a tolerance of ±2° in the horizontal and longitudinal plane at the time of first contact, and with the impactor axis perpendicular to the horizontal plane within a roll and pitch angle tolerance of ±2° in the lateral and longitudinal plane.

The bumper shall meet the lower legform to bumper test requirements with the bottom of the impactor (without parts needed for the purposes of launching and/or protection) at 75 mm ± 10 mm above the ground reference plane at the time of first contact with the bumper.
The bumper shall meet the lower legform to bumper test requirements when struck by the impactor at an impact velocity of 11.1 m/s ± 0.2 m/s.
The impact velocity of the upper legform impactor when striking the bumper shall be 11.1 m/s ± 0.2 m/s.

Where two or more lamps are part of the same unit of grouped, combined or reciprocally incorporated lamps, each of these lamps shall satisfy the provisions set out in UN Regulation No. 148 or in another Regulation.
Lamps not satisfying the provisions of UN Regulation No. 148 or of another Regulation shall not be part of a unit of grouped, combined or reciprocally incorporated lamps.
Every device belonging to an approved type shall comprise a space of sufficient size for the approval marking and other markings as defined in paragraphs 3.3.3.2. to 3.3.3.6.
All markings on the device shall be clearly legible and indelible.
The value for "a" in the size of the approval marking shall be at least 5 mm, with the arrangement of the markings as shown in the examples of Annex 7.
The approval marking shall include the four to six-digit sequential number being part of the approval number prescribed in paragraph 3.2.3.2.
The sequential number shall be placed close to the approval mark.

On lamps which cannot be mounted on either side of the vehicle indiscriminately, the horizontal arrow showing the mounting position shall be directed outwards from the vehicle in the case of direction indicators categories 1, 1a, 1b, 2a, 2b, 11, 11a, 11b, 11c and 12.

On lamps which cannot be mounted on either side of the vehicle indiscriminately, the horizontal arrow showing the mounting position shall be directed outwards from the vehicle in the case of front or rear position lamps and front or rear end-outline marker lamps.

On lamps which cannot be mounted on either side of the vehicle indiscriminately, the horizontal arrow showing the mounting position shall be directed towards the front of the vehicle in the case of direction indicators of categories 5 and 6 and combined parking lamps.
For direction indicators of category 6, an indication "R" or "L" shall be shown on the lamp, indicating the right or left side of the vehicle.
Lamps shall bear the approval marking.
Lamps shall bear the trade name or mark of the applicant.
Lamps, with the exception of lamps with non-replaceable light sources, shall bear a marking indicating the category or categories of light source(s) prescribed.

Lamps, with the exception of lamps with non-replaceable light sources, shall, in the case where the lamp has been approved for LED substitute light source(s), bear a marking indicating the category or categories of the LED substitute light source(s).
Lamps with an electronic light source control gear shall bear marking of the rated voltage(s) (i.e. 6V, 12V or 24V) or the range of voltage.
Lamps with a variable luminous intensity control shall bear marking of the rated voltage(s) (i.e. 6V, 12V or 24V) or the range of voltage.
Lamps with a secondary operating mode shall bear marking of the rated voltage(s) (i.e. 6V, 12V or 24V) or the range of voltage.
Lamps with non-replaceable light sources shall bear marking of the rated voltage(s) (i.e. 6V, 12V or 24V) or the range of voltage.
In case replaceable light source module(s) is/are used, the light source module(s) shall bear the trade name or mark of the applicant.
In case replaceable light source module(s) is/are used, the light source module(s) shall bear the specific identification code of the module.

In case replaceable light source module(s) is/are used, the specific identification code of the light source module shall comprise the starting letters "MD" for "MODULE" followed by the approval mark without the circle.
In case several non-identical light source modules are used, the specific identification code of each light source module shall be followed by additional symbols or characters.
In case replaceable light source modules are used, the approval mark on the light source module and the approval mark on the lamp in which the module is used shall be from the same applicant.
In case replaceable light source module(s) is/are used, the light source module(s) shall bear the rated voltage(s) or the range of voltage.
In case replaceable light source module(s) is/are used, the lamp shall bear the specific identification code of the module as prescribed in paragraph 3.3.3.5. (a), (ii).

An electronic light source control gear or variable luminous intensity control being part of the lamp, but not included into the lamp body, shall be marked with its identification number and the name of the manufacturer.

The approval marking of the lamp shall be placed on an inner or outer part (transparent or not) of the lamp which is not designed to be separated from the transparent part of the lamp emitting the light.

The approval marking of the lamp, as well as the category or categories of LED substitute light source(s) prescribed, if any, shall be visible when the lamp is fitted on the vehicle or when a movable part such as the hood or boot lid or a door is opened.
If the outer lens of a device is designed to be separated from the main body, the approval marking shall be placed on both the detachable lens and the main body.
In case an outer lens is used for several devices and bears different approval markings, the main body of each device shall bear only the approval marking of the function(s) of that device.
The approval marking and the markings in paragraphs 3.3.3.2., 3.3.3.3., 3.3.3.4., 3.3.3.5. (b) and 3.3.3.6. shall be affixed on the lamp.
The markings in paragraph 3.3.3.5.(a) shall be affixed on the component.

Where a single approval mark is affixed to grouped, combined or reciprocally incorporated lamps, the size of the components of the single approval mark shall not be less than the minimum size required for the smallest of the individual marks by the pertinent UN Regulations under which approval has been granted.
Each lamp submitted for approval shall conform to the requirements set forth in paragraphs 4. and 5. of UN Regulation No. 148.

The lamp shall comply with the requirements contained in sections 5 "General specifications" and 6 "Individual specifications" (and in the Annexes referenced in the said sections) of UN Regulations Nos. 48, 53, 74 or 86, and their series of amendments in force at the time of application for the lamp type approval.

The lamp shall comply with the requirements of UN Regulations Nos. 48, 53, 74 or 86 pertinent to each lamp and to the category/ies of vehicle on which the lamp is intended to be installed, where its verification at the moment of lamp type approval is feasible.

The lamps shall be so designed and constructed that in normal conditions of use, and notwithstanding the vibrations to which they may be subjected in such use, their satisfactory operation remains assured and they retain the characteristics prescribed by UN Regulation No. 148.

If a front position lamp incorporates one or more infrared radiation generators, the photometric and colour requirements for this front position lamp shall be met with and without the operation of the infrared radiation generator(s).

Where a manufacturer logo is incorporated in the internal structure of the optical components and/or the texture of the outer lens inside of the apparent surface of a lamp (function), only one manufacturer logo built by transparent or non-transparent components shall be incorporated, provided that all requirements for the specific function of UN Regulation No. 148 are fulfilled.

Where a lamp incorporates a logo, irrespective of the marking requirements in paragraph 3.3., only the logo of the brand name of the vehicle manufacturer or the body manufacturer shall be allowed, as confirmed by the applicant by a statement (see paragraph 3.1.2.2. (f)).

Where a lamp incorporates a logo, the enclosed light emitting surface of the logo (incorporating transparent and non-transparent components of the logo) in the direction of the reference axis shall not exceed 100 cm2.
Stop lamps, direction indicator lamps, and reversing lamps shall not incorporate a logo.

In case of failure of any one light source in a single lamp containing more than one light source, either the light intensity shall comply with the minimum intensity required in the pertinent table of standard light distribution as shown in Annex 3 with the maximum intensities not exceeded when all light sources are illuminated, or a signal for activation of a tell-tale indicating failure, as indicated in paragraphs 6.4.8., 6.7.8., 6.9.8, 6.10.8., 6.11.8., 6.12.8., 6.13.8. and 6.18.8. of UN Regulation No. 48, shall be produced, in which case the lamp is only for use on a vehicle fitted with a tell-tale indicating failure.

For daytime running lamps, in case of failure of any one light source in a single lamp containing more than one light source, either the light intensity at the points of standard light distribution defined in paragraph 2.2. of Annex 3 shall be at least 80 per cent of the minimum intensity required, or a signal for activation of a tell-tale indicating failure, as indicated in paragraph 6.19.8. of UN Regulation No. 48, shall be produced, in which case the lamp is only for use on a vehicle fitted with a tell-tale indicating failure.

For direction-indicator lamps of categories 1, 1a, 1b, 2a, 2b, 11, 11a, 11b, 11c and 12 containing more than one light source, a signal for activation of the tell-tale prescribed in paragraph 6.5.8. of Regulation No. 48 or paragraph 6.3.8. of Regulation No. 53 shall be produced on the basis of either option (a) any one light source has failed, (b) in the case of a lamp designed for only two light sources, the intensity in the axis of reference is less than 50 per cent of the minimum intensity required, or (c) as a consequence of a failure of one or more light sources, the intensity in one of the directions H=0°, V=0°; H=20° outwards to the outside of the vehicle, V=+5°; or H=10° inwards to the inside of the vehicle, V=0°, as indicated in paragraph 2.1. of Annex 3, is less than the minimum intensity required.

The lamp shall only be equipped with replaceable light source(s) approved according to UN Regulations Nos. 37, 99 and/or 128, provided that no restriction on the use is made at the time of application for type approval, and/or light source module(s) and/or non-replaceable light source(s).
In case of replaceable UN approved light source(s), the design of the lamp shall be such that the light source(s) can be fixed in no other position but the correct one.

In case of replaceable UN approved light source(s), the light source(s) holder shall conform to the characteristics given in IEC Publication 60061, the holder data sheet relevant to the category of light source(s) prescribed applying.

In case of replaceable UN approved light source(s) where a category of LED substitute light source(s) is also prescribed, the light source(s) holder shall conform to the holder data sheet of IEC Publication 60061 relevant to the category of LED substitute light source(s).
Light Signalling Devices shall not generate radiated or power line disturbances which cause a malfunction of other electric/electronic systems of the vehicle.

In case of replaceable light source module(s), the design of the light source module(s) shall be such that it can only be fitted in the designated and correct position and can only be removed with the use of tool(s).
In case of replaceable light source module(s), the design of the light source module(s) shall be such that it is tamperproof.

In case of replaceable light source module(s), the design of the light source module(s) shall be such that, regardless of the use of tool(s), it is not interchangeable with any replaceable UN approved light source and/or any other replaceable light source module having different characteristics that is located in the same lamp housing.

In case of replaceable light source module(s), when the light source module is removed and replaced by another module provided by the applicant and bearing the same light source module identification code, the photometric requirements of the device shall be met.

Where the lamp may be installed on the vehicle in more than one or in a field of different positions, the photometric measurements shall be repeated for each position or for the extreme positions of the field of the reference axis specified by the manufacturer.
Unless otherwise specified, the voltage supplied at the lamp for testing shall be 13.5 V for 12 Volt-Systems.
In case of a lamp controlled by an electronic light source control gear or a variable intensity control, the lamp shall be operated for testing as specified by the applicant.

In case of a lamp not controlled by an electronic light source control gear or a variable intensity control and equipped with light source module(s) or non-replaceable light source(s), the lamp shall be operated for testing as specified by the applicant.

In case of lamps equipped with multiple replaceable UN approved light sources operated at a common voltage or electrical current setting, the measured luminous intensities shall be corrected proportionally for the difference between the average luminous flux and the applicable reference/objective luminous flux.

If not otherwise specified, the intensity of light emitted by each of the two samples supplied shall, on the reference axis (HV), be not less than the minimum specified in the table of the pertinent function in paragraph 5.

If not otherwise specified, the intensity of light emitted by each of the two samples supplied shall, in no direction where the lamp is visible, exceed the maximum specified in the table of the pertinent function in paragraph 5.

If not otherwise specified, the intensity of light emitted by each of the two samples supplied shall, outside the reference axis, be not less than the product of the minimum specified in the table of the pertinent function in paragraph 5. by the percentage specified in the pertinent light distribution figure reproduced in Annex 3 for each direction in question, or be not less than the intensity value as specified in the pertinent light distribution figure reproduced in Annex 3 for each direction in question.

If not otherwise specified, the intensity of light emitted by each of the two samples supplied shall, within the angles of geometric visibility defined in the tables in Annex 2, be not less than the minimum specified in the table of the pertinent function in paragraph 5.
The intensity of light emitted by the lamp shall observe the provisions of the relevant paragraphs of Annex 3 on local variations of intensity.

Where the applicant requests the additional test to verify the visibility of red light towards the front and/or white light towards the rear of a vehicle required in UN Regulation No. 48, the maximum intensity of the lamp in the angular field from 165° to 180° outboard in horizontal direction and -2.5° to +5° in vertical direction shall be not more than 2.5∙10-1 cd, the influence of the vehicle body may be taken into account.

Where an assembly of two independent lamps, to be type approved as lamps marked "D" and having the same function, is deemed to be a single lamp, it shall comply with the requirements for maximum intensity if all lamps together are lit.

Where an assembly of two independent lamps, to be type approved as lamps marked "D" and having the same function, is deemed to be a single lamp, it shall comply with the requirements for minimum intensity if either lamp has failed.
An interdependent lamp system shall meet the luminous intensity requirements when all its interdependent lamps are operated together.

Where a variable intensity control is used for systems depending only on daytime and night-time conditions, the variable intensity control shall not generate signals which cause luminous intensities exceeding the respective steady luminous intensity maximum specified in paragraph 5 for the specific lamp under night-time conditions.

Where a variable intensity control is used for systems other than those depending only on daytime and night-time conditions, the variable intensity control shall not generate signals which cause luminous intensities exceeding the respective steady luminous intensity maximum specified in paragraph 5 for the specific lamp under standard conditions (good visibility, meteorological optical range MOR > 2,000 m defined according to WMO, Guide to Meteorological Instruments and Methods of Observation, Sixth Edition, ISBN: 92-63-16008-2, pp 1.9.1/1.9.11, Geneva 1996, and clean lens).
The luminous intensities of the lamp shall comply with the requirements when tested according to Annex 8.

The colour of the light emitted by the lamp shall meet the colorimetric characteristics inside the field of the light distribution grid defined for the specific function in the relevant paragraph of Annex 3, when checked with the test procedure described in paragraph 4.8, with the colorimetric characteristics of lamps equipped with non-replaceable light sources verified with the light sources present in the lamp in accordance with the relevant subparagraphs of paragraph 4.8.
The light emitted by the lamp shall show no sharp variation of colour outside the field of the light distribution grid defined for the specific function in the relevant paragraph of Annex 3.

For lamps (functions) using different light source technologies, the colorimetric characteristics shall comply for each light source technology separately according to the applicable provisions in paragraphs 4.8.1 and 4.8.2.

The light emitted by each of the two samples of front position lamps (A, MA) and front end-outline marker lamps (AM) supplied shall meet the luminous intensity and standard light distribution requirements in Table 3.
The minimum luminous intensity of the front position lamp (A, MA) and front end-outline marker lamp (AM) within the angles of geometric visibility shall comply with Table 3.
The front position lamp (A, MA) and front end-outline marker lamp (AM) shall comply with the failure provisions of paragraph 4.6.
The colour of the light emitted by the front position lamp and front end-outline marker lamp shall be white, except that the lamp identified by symbol MA may be amber.

In case the luminous intensity of the daytime running lamp is intended to be reduced according to the relevant requirements of paragraph 6.19.7. of the 08 or any of the subsequent series of amendments to UN Regulation No. 48, the reduced designed maximum luminous intensity shall not exceed 1.40∙10^2 cd.
The minimum luminous intensity of the daytime running lamp (RL) within the angles of geometric visibility shall comply with Table 6.
The area of the apparent surface in the direction of the axis of reference of the daytime running lamp shall be not less than 25 cm2 and not more than 200 cm2.
When a daytime running lamp is to be type approved as a lamp marked "D", the apparent surface of such a lamp shall not be more than 100 cm2.
The daytime running lamp shall be subjected to, and meet, the heat resistance test specified in Annex 6.
The daytime running lamp (RL) shall comply with the failure provisions of paragraph 4.6.
The colour of the light emitted by the daytime running lamp shall be white.
The light emitted by each of the two samples of the direction indicator lamp supplied shall meet the requirements in Table 8.
For direction indicators of categories 1, 1a, 1b, 2a, 2b, 11, 11a, 11b, 11c and 12, the minimum luminous intensities of Table 8 shall be fulfilled in the reference axis.
For direction indicators of categories 5 and 6, the minimum luminous intensities of Table 8 shall be fulfilled in direction A according to Annex 2.
The direction indicator lamp shall meet the minimum luminous intensity within the angles of geometric visibility specified in Table 8.

Where the flash of a direction indicator lamp of category 1, 1a, 1b, 2a, 2b, 11, 11a, 11b, 11c or 12 is produced by sequential activation of its light sources, each light source, after its activation, shall remain lit until the end of the ON cycle.

Where the flash of a direction indicator lamp of category 1, 1a, 1b, 2a, 2b, 11, 11a, 11b, 11c or 12 is produced by sequential activation of its light sources, the sequence of activation of the light sources shall produce a signal which proceeds in a uniform progressive manner from inboard towards the outboard edge of the light emitting surface.

Where the flash of a direction indicator lamp of category 1, 1a, 1b, 2a, 2b, 11, 11a, 11b, 11c or 12 is produced by sequential activation of its light sources, the signal shall be one signal with no interruption and no vertical oscillations (e.g. not more than one change of direction along the vertical axis).

For a sequential direction indicator, the distance between two adjacent/tangential distinct parts of the light emitting surface shall not exceed 50 mm, when measured perpendicularly to the reference axis, instead of the values defined in paragraph 5.7.2. of UN Regulation No. 48 or paragraph 5.7.2. of UN Regulation No. 86 or paragraph 5.6.2. of UN Regulation No. 53.

For a sequential direction indicator, the interruptions of the signal between distinct parts of the light emitting surface shall not create any overlap in the vertical axis between the different parts, from inboard towards the outboard of the vehicle.
For a sequential direction indicator, the interruptions of the signal between distinct parts of the light emitting surface shall not be used for any other lighting or light signalling functions.

Where the flash of a direction indicator lamp of category 1, 1a, 1b, 2a, 2b, 11, 11a, 11b, 11c or 12 is produced by sequential activation of its light sources, the variation shall finish no more than 200 ms after the beginning of the ON cycle.

Where the flash of a direction indicator lamp of category 1, 1a, 1b, 2a, 2b, 11, 11a, 11b, 11c or 12 is produced by sequential activation of its light sources, the orthogonal projection of the light emitting surfaces of the direction indicator in the direction of the axis of reference shall be circumscribed by a rectangle on a plane normal to the axis of reference with its longer sides parallel to the H-plane and a ratio of the horizontal to the vertical sides not less than 1.7.
Where the flash of a direction indicator lamp is produced by sequential activation of its light sources, compliance with the sequential activation conditions shall be verified in flashing mode.
The colour of light emitted by the direction indicator lamp shall be amber.
The light emitted by each of the two samples of the side marker lamp (SM1, SM2) supplied shall meet the requirements in Table 9.
The side marker lamp (SM1, SM2) shall meet the minimum luminous intensity within the angles of geometric visibility specified in Table 9.
The SM1 and SM2 category side marker lamps shall comply with the failure provisions of paragraph 4.6.

The colour of the light emitted by the SM1 and SM2 category side marker lamps shall be amber, except that it can be red if the rearmost side marker lamp is grouped or combined or reciprocally incorporated with the rear position lamp, the rear end-outline marker lamp, the rear fog lamp, the stop lamp, or is grouped with or has part of the light emitting surface in common with the rear retro-reflector.

Unless specified otherwise, the light intensity of the lamp in the various directions of measurement shall meet the minimum intensities given in Figures A3-I to A3-XV as a percentage of the minimum intensities required, mathematically rounded down to three significant digits, with the direction H = 0° and V = 0° corresponding to the reference axis passing through the centre of reference.

Where a front or rear direction indicator lamp, front or rear position lamp, front or rear end-outline marker lamp, parking lamp, stop lamp of category S1, S2 or MS, or side marker lamp is intended to be installed at a mounting height (using the H plane specified by the manufacturer) equal to or less than 750 mm above the ground, the photometric intensity shall be met only up to an angle of 5° downwards.

Within the field of light distribution schematically shown as a grid, the light intensity of the lamp in each direction of a part of the field formed by the grid lines shall meet at least the lowest minimum value shown as a percentage on the grid lines surrounding the questioned direction.

Front and rear position lamps, parking lamps, front and rear end-outline marker lamps, stop lamps (S1, S2 and MS) and direction indicator lamps of categories 1, 1a, 1b, 2a, 2b, 11, 11a, 11b, 11c and 12 shall meet, for the various directions of measurement, the minimum intensities of the standard light distribution given as a percentage of the minimum intensities required in Tables 3, 4, 5, 7 and 8.

Daytime running lamps shall meet, for the various directions of measurement, the minimum intensities of the standard light distribution given as a percentage of the minimum intensity required in Table 6.

Direction indicator lamps of category 6 shall meet, for the various directions of measurement, the minimum intensities of the standard light distribution given as a percentage of the minimum intensity required in Table 8, with the direction H = 5° and V = 0° corresponding to the minimum value prescribed in Table 8.
The chromaticity coordinates of the lamp shall be complied with when tested under the conditions of paragraph 4.9. of UN R148.

Mass-produced lamps shall be considered to conform from a mechanical and a geometric standpoint, in accordance with the requirements of this Regulation, if any, if the differences do not exceed inevitable manufacturing deviations.

For mass-produced lamps chosen at random and tested for the photometric performances set forth in paragraph 4.8. of this Regulation, no measured value shall deviate from the values prescribed in paragraph 6.1.3. of this Regulation.

The lamp shall withstand a one-hour test of continuous operation following a warm-up period of 20 minutes at an ambient temperature of 23 °C ± 5 °C, with a light source of the category specified for the lamp supplied with a current at a voltage such that it gives the specified average power at the corresponding test voltage.

For lamps equipped with non-replaceable light sources (filament light sources and other), the one-hour continuous operation test shall be made with the light sources present in the lamp, in accordance with paragraph 5.4.5. of this Regulation.
Where only the maximum power is specified, the heat resistance test of the lamp shall be carried out by regulating the voltage to obtain a power equal to 90 per cent of the specified power.
The specified average or maximum power for the heat resistance test shall in all cases be chosen from the rated voltage(s) of 6, 12 or 24 V at which it reaches the highest value.
For lamps equipped with non-replaceable light sources, the heat resistance test conditions set in paragraph 5.4.5. or 5.9.5. of this Regulation shall be applied.

In the case of light sources operated by an electronic control gear to obtain variable luminous intensity, the heat resistance test of the lamp shall be carried out under the conditions given at minimum 90 per cent of the higher luminous intensity.
After the heat resistance test and after the lamp has been stabilized at the ambient temperature, no distortion, deformation, cracking or colour modification of the lamp shall be perceptible.

In case of doubt, the intensity of light of the lamp measured according to paragraph 5. of this Regulation after the heat resistance test shall reach at least 90 per cent of the values obtained before the heat resistance test on the same lamp.
For lamps (functions) using incandescent technology only, the luminous intensities measured after photometric stability shall comply with the minimum and maximum requirements.

For lamps (functions) using light source technologies other than incandescent technology, other than those covered by the specific provisions for particular lamps, the luminous intensities measured after 1 min and either after 30 minutes of operation or after photometric stability has occurred shall comply with the minimum and maximum requirements, with direction indicator lamps operated in flashing mode (f = 1.5 Hz, duty factor 50 per cent).

In case a lamp (function) uses any other light generating technology, the lamp (function) shall comply with the corresponding intensity requirements at the corresponding point in time listed in Table A8-1 and up to when photometric stability is reached.

In case a lamp (function) uses more than one light generating technology, the lamp (function) shall comply with the corresponding intensity requirements when tested following the strictest time requirements according to paragraphs 2.1.1. to 2.1.3. for the combination of them.

In case of doubt (e.g. unexpected run-up behaviour), the lamp (function) shall comply with the corresponding minimum intensity requirements at all points in time starting at the corresponding point in time listed in Table A8-1 and ending when photometric stability is reached.

The external surface of vehicles shall not exhibit, directed outwards, any pointed or sharp parts or any projections of such shape, dimensions, direction or hardness as to be likely to increase the risk or seriousness of bodily injury to a person hit by the external surface or brushing against it in the event of a collision.
The external surface of vehicles shall not exhibit, directed outwards, any part likely to catch on pedestrians, cyclists or motor cyclists.
No protruding part of the external surface shall have a radius of curvature less than 2.5 mm, except for parts of the external surface which protrude less than 5 mm.
The outward facing angles of parts of the external surface which protrude less than 5 mm shall be blunted, save where such parts protrude less than 1.5 mm.

Protruding parts of the external surface made of a material of hardness not exceeding 60 Shore A, with the hardness measured with the component as installed on the vehicle (or by comparable measurements where the Shore A procedure is impossible), may have a radius of curvature less than 2.5 mm.

Added ornaments which project more than 10 mm from their support shall retract, become detached or bend over under a force of 10 daN exerted at their most salient point in any direction in a plane approximately parallel to the surface on which they are mounted, except ornaments on radiator grilles, to which only the general requirements of paragraph 5. shall apply.
After added ornaments are retracted, detached or bent over, the remaining projections shall not project more than 10 mm.
The remaining projections of added ornaments after retraction, detachment or bending over shall in any case satisfy the provisions of paragraph 5.2.
Protective strips or shielding on the external surface shall be firmly secured to the vehicle.

Gaps between fixed or movable elements, including those forming part of air intake or outlet grilles and radiator grilles, shall be exempt from the requirements of paragraph 5.4. only provided that the distance between consecutive elements does not exceed 40 mm and the grilles and gaps have a functional purpose.
For gaps of between 40 mm and 25 mm between consecutive elements of grilles and gaps, the radii of curvature shall be 1 mm or more.
If the distance between two consecutive elements of grilles and gaps is equal to or less than 25 mm, the radii of curvature of external faces of the elements shall not be less than 0.5 mm.
The junction of the front with the side faces of each element forming a grille or gap shall be blunted.

The ends of the bumpers shall be turned in towards the external surface in order to minimize the risk of fouling, which is considered satisfied if either the bumper is recessed or integrated within the bodywork or the end of the bumper is turned in so that it is not contactable by a 100 mm sphere and the gap between the bumper end and the surrounding bodywork does not exceed 20 mm.

If the line of the bumper which corresponds to the outline contour of the car vertical projection is on a rigid surface, that surface shall have a minimum radius of curvature of 5 mm at all its points lying from the contour line to 20 mm inward, in that part of the zone situated between and in front (or rear in case of the rear bumper) of the tangential points with the contour line of two vertical planes each forming an angle of 15° with the longitudinal plane of symmetry of the vehicle.

If the line of the bumper which corresponds to the outline contour of the car vertical projection is on a rigid surface, that surface shall have a minimum radius of curvature of 2.5 mm in all other cases.

Parts on or of the bumper or bumper insets which have a projection of less than 5 mm, with special reference to joint covers and jets for headlamp washers, shall have their outward facing angles blunted, save where such parts protrude less than 1.5 mm.

The projection of handles, hinges and push-buttons of doors, luggage compartments and bonnets and of fuel tank filler caps and covers shall not exceed 30 mm in all cases other than door or luggage compartment handles.

Folds in body panels with a radius of curvature of less than 2.5 mm shall have a radius of curvature not less than one-tenth of the height "H" of the projection, measured in accordance with the method described in paragraph 1. of Annex 3.
Air intake and outlet flaps shall meet the requirements of paragraphs 5.2., 5.3. and 5.4. of UN R26 in all positions of use.

Supporting brackets provided by the vehicle manufacturer for registration plates shall comply with the requirements of paragraph 5.4. of UN R26 if they are contactable by a 100 mm diameter sphere when a registration plate is fitted in accordance with the vehicle manufacturer's recommendation.

Radio receiving and transmitting aerials shall be fitted to the vehicle in such a way that, if their unattached end is less than 2 m from the road surface in any position of use specified by the manufacturer of the aerial, the unattached end is inside the zone bounded by the vertical planes which are 10 cm inside the extreme outer edge of the vehicle as defined in paragraph 2.7. of UN R26.

Aerials shall be so fitted to the vehicle, and if necessary their unattached ends so restricted, that no part of the aerials protrudes beyond the extreme outer edge of the vehicle as defined in paragraph 2.7. of UN R26.
The unattached ends of aerials shall be fitted with fixed cappings the radii of curvature of which are not less than 2.5 mm, while shafts of aerials may have radii of curvature of less than 2.5 mm.
The bases of aerials shall not project more than 40 mm when determined according to the procedure of paragraph 2. of Annex 3 to UN R26.

Where, by the absence of a flexible shaft or part, it is not possible to identify the base of an aerial, the aerial shall, after a horizontal force of not more than 50 daN in forward and rearward direction is applied by a flat-ended ram of not more than 50 mm diameter at the most salient part of the aerial, either (a) bend towards the support and not project more than 40 mm, or (b) break off with the remaining part of the aerial not showing any sharp or dangerous part that can be contacted by the 100 mm sphere and not projecting more than 40 mm.

After each impact test made in accordance with the conditions and procedure specified in annex 3, the lighting and signalling devices of the vehicle shall continue to operate correctly and remain visible, whereby disturbed adjustment of factory-fitted lighting devices may be corrected to conform to the required specifications only if this can be done by the normal means of adjustment, and bulbs may be replaced only in the event of filament failure.
After each impact test made in accordance with the conditions and procedure specified in annex 3, the vehicle's bonnet (hood), boot lid (trunk lid) and doors shall be operable in the normal manner.
After each impact test made in accordance with the conditions and procedure specified in annex 3, the side doors of the vehicle shall not be able to open under the effect of the impact.

After each impact test made in accordance with the conditions and procedure specified in annex 3, the vehicle's fuel and cooling systems shall have neither leaks nor constricted fluid passages which prevent normal functioning.

After each impact test made in accordance with the conditions and procedure specified in annex 3, the sealing devices and caps of the vehicle's fuel and cooling systems shall be operable in the normal manner.

After each impact test made in accordance with the conditions and procedure specified in annex 3, the vehicle's propulsion, suspension (including tyres), steering and braking systems shall remain in adjustment and shall operate in a normal manner, except that sensors, cameras, radar devices, etc. being part of driver assist systems may become damaged, disoriented or broken due to the impact as long as the basic braking and steering performance are still intact.
The first contact of the impactor with the vehicle shall be by the impact contour on the protective device.

In the two vehicle-loading conditions, the protective device between the corners, as defined in paragraph 3.1.5. of UN R42, shall be intersected by the horizontal plane passing through the reference line of the impactor.
The reference height of the impactor (striker) for the protective device impact tests shall be 445 mm.

For the longitudinal impacts on the front and rear surfaces, the protective device shall withstand a first impact at a freely chosen impactor location and a second impact with the median plane of the impactor at a distance of at least 300 mm from the first, provided that during these impacts the extremities of the impactor do not pass outside a zone defined by two planes parallel to the longitudinal median plane and passing through the corners of the vehicle.
For the longitudinal impact test, the protective device shall be impacted with the impactor placed so that plane A is vertical and the reference line is horizontal at the reference height of 445 mm.
For the corner impact test, the protective device shall be impacted with the impactor placed so that plane A is vertical and the reference line is horizontal and at the reference height of 445 mm.

The lighting and light-signalling devices shall be so fitted that under normal conditions of use as defined in paragraphs 2.3.10., 2.3.10.1. and 2.3.10.2. and notwithstanding any vibrations to which they may be subjected, they retain the characteristics prescribed by UN R48 and enable the vehicle to comply with the requirements of UN R48.
The lighting and light-signalling devices shall be so fitted that it is not possible for the lamps to be inadvertently maladjusted.

For all light-signalling devices, including those mounted on the side panels, the reference axis of the lamp when fitted to the vehicle shall be parallel to the bearing plane of the vehicle on the road, with a tolerance of ±3°.

For side retro-reflectors and side-marker lamps, the reference axis of the lamp when fitted to the vehicle shall be perpendicular to the median longitudinal plane of the vehicle, with a tolerance of ±3°.

For all light-signalling devices other than side retro-reflectors and side-marker lamps, the reference axis of the lamp when fitted to the vehicle shall be parallel to the median longitudinal plane of the vehicle, with a tolerance of ±3°.
Any specific instructions as regards fitting of light-signalling devices laid down by the manufacturer shall be complied with.
In the absence of specific instructions, lamps constituting a pair shall have substantially identical photometric characteristics, except for a matched pair of a function and/or an AFS.
On vehicles whose external shape is asymmetrical, the lamp installation requirements shall be satisfied so far as is possible.

Lamps that are grouped, combined or reciprocally incorporated with one another shall fulfil all requirements regarding colour, position, orientation, geometric visibility, electrical connections and other requirements, if any.
The photometric and colorimetric requirements of a lamp shall be fulfilled when all other functions with which this lamp is grouped, combined or reciprocally incorporated are switched OFF.

When a front or rear position lamp is reciprocally incorporated with one or more other function(s) which can be switched ON together with them, the requirements regarding colour of each of these other functions shall be fulfilled when the reciprocally incorporated function(s) and the front or rear position lamps are switched ON.

Single lamps as defined in paragraph 2.14.11.1., subparagraph (a), the apparent surface of which is composed of two or more distinct parts, other than a single retro-reflector, shall be installed in such a way that either (a) the total area of the projection of the distinct parts of the apparent surface in the direction of the reference axis on a plane tangent to the exterior surface of the outer lens and perpendicular to the reference axis occupies not less than 60 per cent of the smallest quadrilateral circumscribing the projection of the said apparent surface in the direction of the reference axis, or (b) the minimum distance between the facing edges of two adjacent/tangential distinct parts of the apparent surface in the direction of the reference axis does not exceed 75 mm when measured perpendicularly to the reference axis.

Single lamps as defined in paragraph 2.4.11.1., subparagraph (b) or (c), composed of two lamps marked "D" or two independent retro reflectors, shall be installed in such a way that either (a) the projection of the apparent surfaces in the direction of the reference axis of the two lamps or retro reflectors occupies not less than 60 per cent of the smallest quadrilateral circumscribing the projections of the said apparent surfaces in the direction of the reference axis, or (b) the minimum distance between the facing edges of the apparent surfaces in the direction of the reference axis of two lamps or two independent retro reflectors does not exceed 75 mm when measured perpendicularly to the reference axis.
Single lamps as defined in paragraph 2.4.11.1., subparagraph (d) shall fulfil the requirements of paragraph 5.7.2.1.

Where two or more lamps and/or two or more separate apparent surfaces are included into the same lamp body and/or have a common outer lens, these shall not be considered as an interdependent lamp system, except that a lamp in the shape of a band or strip may be part of an interdependent lamp system.

Two lamps or an even number of lamps in the shape of a band or strip shall be placed symmetrically in relation to the median longitudinal plane of the vehicle, extending on both sides to within at least 0.4 m of the extreme outer edge of the vehicle, and shall be not less than 0.8 m long.
The illumination of the surface of two lamps or an even number of lamps in the shape of a band or strip shall be provided by not less than two light sources placed as close as possible to the ends.

Where the light-emitting surface of two lamps or an even number of lamps in the shape of a band or strip is constituted by a number of juxtaposed elements, these individual light-emitting surfaces, when projected on a transverse plane, shall fulfil the requirements of paragraph 5.7.2.1.
The maximum height above the ground of a lamp shall be determined from the highest point and the minimum height from the lowest point of the apparent surface in the direction of the reference axis.

In the absence of specific instructions, the photometric characteristics (e.g. intensity, colour, apparent surface, etc.) of a lamp shall not be intentionally varied during the period when the lamp is switched ON.
Direction-indicator lamps shall be flashing lamps.
The vehicle-hazard warning signal shall be a flashing signal.
Amber side-marker lamps complying with paragraph 6.18.7. shall be flashing lamps.
The emergency stop signal shall be a flashing signal.

Where the photometric characteristics of any lamp vary in relation to the ambient light, as a consequence of other lamps being switched ON or OFF, or when the lamp is being used to provide another lighting function, any variation in the photometric characteristics shall be in compliance with the technical provisions for the lamp concerned.

Where the photometric characteristics of a direction indicator lamp of categories 1, 1a, 1b, 2a or 2b are varied during a flash, the variation shall be by sequential activation of light sources as specified in paragraph 5.6. of UN Regulation No. 6 or paragraph 5.6.11. of UN Regulation No. [LSD].
Sequential activation of light sources shall not be applied when direction indicator lamps of categories 2a and 2b are operated as emergency stop signal according to paragraph 6.23.1.

The lamp(s) used for answer-back signal, which may flash and/or vary in luminous intensity and/or vary in apparent surface, shall operate according to the conditions specified in general specifications and/or in dedicated paragraph 6.27.
White light emitted by a lamp fitted on the front of the vehicle (as defined in paragraph 2.1.5.) shall not be visible from the rear of the vehicle.

With the exception of reversing lamps and white side conspicuity markings, there shall be no direct visibility of the apparent surface of a white lamp if viewed by an observer moving within Zone 2 in a transverse plane situated 25 m behind the vehicle (see Annex 4).

In case of doubt, the requirement that no red light be visible from the front and no white light be visible from the rear shall be deemed fulfilled if the luminous intensity of the red light emitted to the front and/or the white light emitted to the rear, as verified during type approval of the lamps, is not more than 0.25 cd per lamp, taking into account the influence of the vehicle body if applicable.

The electrical connections shall be such that the front and rear position lamps, the end-outline marker lamps, if they exist, the side-marker lamps, if they exist, and the rear registration plate lamp can only be switched ON and OFF simultaneously.
In the case of an interdependent lamp system, all light sources shall be switched ON and OFF simultaneously.
The concealment of lamps shall be prohibited, with the exception of the main-beam headlamps, the dipped-beam headlamps and the front fog lamps, which may be concealed when they are not in use.
The colour of the light emitted by the front fog lamp shall be white or selective yellow.
The colour of the light emitted by the direction-indicator lamp shall be amber.
The colour of the light emitted by the hazard warning signal shall be amber.
The colour of the light emitted by the emergency stop signal shall be amber or red.
The colour of the light emitted by the front position lamp shall be white.
The colour of the light emitted by the parking lamp shall be white in front, red at the rear, and amber if reciprocally incorporated in the side direction-indicator lamps or in the side-marker lamps.

The colour of the light emitted by the side-marker lamp shall be amber; however the rearmost side-marker lamp can be red if it is grouped or combined or reciprocally incorporated with the rear position lamp, the rear end-outline marker lamp, the rear fog lamp, the stop lamp or is grouped or has part of the light emitting surface in common with the rear retro-reflector.
The colour of the light emitted by the end-outline marker lamp shall be white in front and red at the rear.
The colour of the light emitted by the daytime running lamp shall be white.
The colour of the front retro-reflector, non-triangular, shall be identical to incident light (also known as white or colourless retro-reflector).

The colour of the side retro-reflector, non-triangular, shall be amber; however the rearmost side retro-reflector can be red if it is grouped or has part of the light emitting surface in common with the rear position lamp, the rear end outline marker lamp, the rear fog lamp, the stop-lamp, the red rearmost side-marker lamp or the rear retro-reflector, non-triangular.
The colour of the light emitted by the cornering lamp shall be white.

The colour of the light emitted by the exterior courtesy lamp shall be white and, in addition, in accordance with the individual specifications applicable to the specific lamp used for the exterior courtesy lamp.
The colour of the light emitted by the manoeuvring lamp shall be white.
The colour of the light emitted by the answer-back signal shall be in accordance with the individual specifications applicable to the specific lamp used for the answer-back signal.
The number of lamps mounted on the vehicle shall be equal to the number indicated in the individual specifications of UN Regulation No. 48.

Lamps approved with light source(s) according to UN Regulation No. 37, except when such light sources are used as non-replaceable light source(s) as defined in paragraph 2.9.1.2., shall be fitted in a vehicle in such a way that the light source can be correctly replaced without the need for expert assistance and without the need for special tools, other than those provided with the vehicle by the manufacturer.

In the case where a light source module includes a holder for an approved replaceable light source according to Regulation No. 37, this light source shall be replaceable without the need for expert assistance and without the need for special tools, other than those provided with the vehicle by the manufacturer.

For vehicles of M and N categories, when the electrical system of the vehicle is in a constant voltage operating condition representative for the relevant category of powered vehicle as specified by the applicant, the voltage supplied at the terminals of devices indicated in 2.5.1., 2.5.2., 2.5.4., 2.5.6. and 2.5.7. which, according to their type approval documentation, have been tested by the application of a special power supply/electronic light source control gear, or in a secondary operating mode or at a voltage requested by the applicant, shall not exceed the voltage specified for the relevant devices or functions as they have been approved.

For vehicles of M and N categories with 6 Volt-Systems, in all cases of electric power supply conditions not covered by the special power supply/secondary operating mode/applicant-requested voltage provision, the voltage at the terminals of the device(s) or function(s) indicated in 2.5.1., 2.5.2., 2.5.4., 2.5.6. and 2.5.7. shall not exceed 6.75 V by more than 3 per cent when the electrical system of the vehicle is in a constant voltage operating condition.

There shall be no obstacle on the inside of the angles of geometric visibility to the propagation of light from any part of the apparent surface of the lamp observed from infinity, except obstacles that were already presented when the lamp was type-approved.

If, when the lamp is installed, any part of the apparent surface of the lamp is hidden by any further parts of the vehicle, the part of the lamp not hidden by obstacles shall still conform to the photometric values prescribed for the approval of the device.

Where the vertical angle of geometric visibility below the horizontal may be reduced to 5° (lamp at less than 750 mm above the ground measured according to the provisions of paragraph 5.8.1.), the photometric field of measurements of the installed optical unit may be reduced to 5° below the horizontal.
In the case of an interdependent lamp system, the geometric visibility requirements shall be fulfilled when all its interdependent lamps are operated together.

All lamps (devices) installed on a vehicle shall, where applicable, be type approved according to the corresponding device Regulations as specified in the relevant subparagraphs of paragraph 6 of UN Regulation No. 48.
Light-signalling lamps incorporating a manufacturer logo shall be type approved according to the requirements of UN Regulation No. 148.

Lamps installed on a vehicle approved according to UN Regulation No. 48 and approved for one or more replaceable light source categories according to Regulations Nos. 37, 99 or 128 shall be fitted with light sources approved according to these light source categories only, this requirement not concerning light source modules, LED modules and non-replaceable light sources except for when they are required to be approved by the applicable Regulation.

Lamps approved for and equipped with LED substitute light source(s) shall be used exclusively in the case where the statement indicated in paragraph 3.2.8. is present and positive, and such lamps shall bear the marking related to the use of LED substitute light source(s).
The presence of direction-indicator lamps shall be mandatory.
Arrangement "A" of direction-indicator lamps (categories 1, 1a, 1b, 2a, 2b, 5 and 6) shall apply to all motor vehicles.
The number of direction-indicator lamps shall be according to the arrangement.

Direction-indicator lamps shall be type-approved according to the 01 or subsequent series of amendments to UN Regulation No. 6, or to the 00 or subsequent series of amendments to UN Regulation No. 148.

For arrangement A, the two front direction-indicator lamps shall be of category 1 or 1a or 1b if the distance between the edge of the apparent surface in the direction of the reference axis of this lamp and that of the apparent surface in the direction of the reference axis of the dipped-beam headlamp and/or the front fog lamp, if there is one, is at least 40 mm.
