For arrangement A, the two front direction-indicator lamps shall be of category 1a or 1b if the distance between the edge of the apparent surface in the direction of the reference axis of this lamp and that of the apparent surface in the direction of the reference axis of the dipped-beam headlamp and/or the front fog lamp, if there is one, is greater than 20 mm and less than 40 mm.

For arrangement A, the two front direction-indicator lamps shall be of category 1b if the distance between the edge of the apparent surface in the direction of the reference axis of this lamp and that of the apparent surface in the direction of the reference axis of the dipped-beam headlamp and/or the front fog lamp, if there is one, is less than or equal to 20 mm.

For arrangement A, two side direction-indicator lamps of category 5 (minimum requirement) shall be fitted for all M1 vehicles and for N1, M2 and M3 vehicles not exceeding 6 metres in length, category 5 side direction-indicator lamps being permitted to be replaced by category 6 side direction-indicator lamps in all instances.

Where lamps combining the functions of front direction-indicator lamps (categories 1, 1a, 1b) and side direction-indicator lamps (categories 5 or 6) are fitted, two additional side direction-indicator lamps (categories 5 or 6) may be fitted to meet the visibility requirements of paragraph 6.5.5.

Where an AFS is fitted, the distance to be considered for the choice of the front direction-indicator lamp category shall be the distance between the front direction-indicator lamp and the closest lighting unit in its closest position contributing to or performing a passing-beam mode.

The edge of the apparent surface of the direction-indicator lamp in the direction of the reference axis farthest from the median longitudinal plane of the vehicle shall not be more than 400 mm from the extreme outer edge of the vehicle, except for the optional rear lamps.

The distance between the inner edges of the two apparent surfaces of the direction-indicator lamps in the direction of the reference axes shall not be less than 600 mm, or not less than 400 mm where the overall width of the vehicle is less than 1,300 mm.

The height above the ground of the light-emitting surface of the side direction-indicator lamps of categories 5 or 6 shall not be less than 350 mm for M1 and N1 category of vehicles and 500 mm for all other categories of vehicles, measured from the lowest point.
The height above the ground of the light-emitting surface of the side direction-indicator lamps of categories 5 or 6 shall not be more than 1,500 mm, measured from the highest point.
The height above the ground of the direction-indicator lamps of categories 1, 1a, 1b, 2a and 2b, measured in accordance with paragraph 5.8., shall not be less than 350 mm and not more than 1,500 mm.

If the structure of the vehicle does not permit the upper height limits to be respected and if the optional rear lamps are not installed, the upper height limit may be increased to 2,300 mm for side direction-indicator lamps of categories 5 and 6.

If the structure of the vehicle does not permit the upper height limits to be respected and if the optional rear lamps are not installed, the upper height limit may be increased to 2,100 mm for the direction-indicator lamps of categories 1, 1a, 1b, 2a and 2b.

The distance between the light-emitting surface of the side direction-indicator lamp (categories 5 and 6) and the transverse plane which marks the forward boundary of the vehicle's overall length shall not exceed 1,800 mm, except as permitted for 2,500 mm.

For M1 and N1 category vehicles, the distance between the light-emitting surface of the side direction-indicator lamp (categories 5 and 6) and the transverse plane which marks the forward boundary of the vehicle's overall length shall not exceed 2,500 mm.

The direction indicator lamps of categories 1, 1a, 1b, 2a, 2b and 5 shall have vertical angles of geometric visibility of 15° above and below the horizontal, except that the downward angle of 15° may be reduced to 5° where a lamp is mounted below 750 mm (measured according to the provisions of paragraph 5.8.1).

The direction indicator lamps shall comply with the horizontal angles of geometric visibility shown in the figure of paragraph 6.5.5.1, with the value of 5° for the dead angle of visibility to the rear of the side direction-indicator being an upper limit for d ≤ 1.80 m (for M1 and N1 category vehicles d ≤ 2.50 m).

For the direction indicator lamps of categories 1, 1a, 1b, 2a and 2b mounted below 750 mm (measured according to the provisions of paragraph 5.8.1), the inward angle of 45° may be reduced to 20° under the H plane.

At the discretion of the manufacturer, for M1 and N1 category vehicles, the front and rear direction indicator lamps, as well as side-marker lamps, shall comply with the horizontal angles of geometric visibility shown in the figure of paragraph 6.5.5.2, with the value of 5° for the dead angle of visibility to the rear of the side direction-indicator being an upper limit for d ≤ 2.50 m.

Under the alternative of paragraph 6.5.5.2 for M1 and N1 category vehicles, for the direction indicator lamps of categories 1, 1a, 1b, 2a and 2b mounted below 750 mm (measured according to the provisions of paragraph 5.8.1), the inward angle of 45° may be reduced to 20° under the H plane.

Under the alternative of paragraph 6.5.5.2 for M1 and N1 category vehicles, the direction indicator lamps and side-marker lamps shall have vertical angles of geometric visibility of 15° above and below the horizontal, except that the downward angle of 15° may be reduced to 5° where a lamp is mounted below 750 mm (measured according to the provisions of paragraph 5.8.1).

Under the alternative of paragraph 6.5.5.2 for M1 and N1 category vehicles, to be considered visible the lamp shall provide an unobstructed view of the apparent surface of at least 12.5 square centimetres, except for side direction-indicators of categories 5 and 6, with the illuminating surface area of any retro-reflector that does not transmit light excluded.
Direction-indicator lamps shall switch ON independently of the other lamps.
All direction-indicator lamps on one side of a vehicle shall be switched ON and OFF automatically as defined by applicable UN Regulations and/or by means of one control.
All direction-indicator lamps on one side of a vehicle shall flash in phase.

On M1 and N1 vehicles less than 6 m in length, with an arrangement complying with paragraph 6.5.5.2., the amber side-marker lamps, when mounted, shall also flash at the same frequency (in phase) with the direction-indicator lamps.
A direction indicator capable of being activated in different modes (static or sequential) shall not switch between both modes once activated.
An operating tell-tale, visual or auditory or both, shall be provided for direction-indicator lamps of categories 1, 1a, 1b, 2a and 2b.

If the direction-indicator operating tell-tale is visual, it shall be a flashing light which, at least in the event of the malfunction of any of the direction-indicator lamps of categories 1, 1a, 1b, 2a and 2b, is either extinguished, or remains alight without flashing, or shows a marked change of frequency.

If the direction-indicator operating tell-tale is entirely auditory, it shall be clearly audible and shall show a marked change of frequency, at least in the event of the malfunction of any of the direction-indicator lamps of categories 1, 1a, 1b, 2a and 2b.

The direction-indicator operating tell-tale shall be activated by the signal produced according to paragraph 6.2.2. of UN Regulation No. 6, or paragraph 5.6.3. of the 00 series of amendments to UN Regulation No. 148, or paragraph 4.6.1.4. of the 01 series of amendments to UN Regulation No. 148, or another suitable way.
The direction-indicator lamp light shall be a flashing light flashing 90 ± 30 times per minute.

Operation of the direction-indicator light-signal control shall be followed within not more than one second by the emission of light and within not more than one and one-half seconds by its first extinction.

In the event of failure, other than short-circuit, of one direction-indicator lamp, the other direction-indicator lamps shall continue to flash, but the frequency in this condition may be different from that prescribed.
The hazard warning signal shall be mandatory.
The hazard warning signal shall be given by simultaneous operation of the direction-indicator lamps in accordance with the requirements of paragraph 6.5.
All direction indicators of the category 1 (1, 1a, 1b) activated simultaneously for the hazard warning signal shall operate in the same mode, i.e. static or sequential.
The position in width of the hazard warning signal lamps shall be as specified in paragraph 6.5.4.1.
The position in height of the hazard warning signal lamps shall be as specified in paragraph 6.5.4.2.
The position in length of the hazard warning signal lamps shall be as specified in paragraph 6.5.4.3.

Where the hazard warning signal is switched ON automatically to indicate to other road-users the risk of imminent danger as defined by Regulations, the signal shall remain switched ON until it is manually or automatically switched OFF.
The hazard warning signal shall be able to function even if the device which starts or stops the propulsion system is in a position which makes it impossible to start the propulsion system.
The front position lamp shall be mandatory on all motor vehicles.

For the front position lamp, the point on the apparent surface in the direction of the reference axis which is farthest from the vehicle's median longitudinal plane shall not be more than 400 mm from the extreme outer edge of the vehicle.

The front position lamp shall be mounted in height above the ground not less than 250 mm nor more than 1,500 mm (2,100 mm for O1 and O2 categories of vehicles, or if for any other categories of vehicles the shape of the bodywork makes it impossible to keep within 1,500 mm).

Where the front position lamp and another lamp are reciprocally incorporated, the apparent surface in the direction of the reference axis of the other lamp shall be used to verify compliance with the front position lamp positioning requirements in width, height and length.
The horizontal angle of geometric visibility of the front position lamp shall be 45° inwards and 80° outwards.

Where the front position lamp is mounted below 750 mm (measured according to the provisions of paragraph 5.8.1.), the inward horizontal angle of geometric visibility of 45° may be reduced to 20° under the H plane.
The vertical angle of geometric visibility of the front position lamp shall be 15° above and below the horizontal.
Where the front position lamp is mounted below 750 mm (measured according to the provisions of paragraph 5.8.1.), the downward vertical angle of geometric visibility of 15° may be reduced to 5°.

For M1 and N1 category vehicles, as an alternative at the discretion of the manufacturer and only if a front side-marker lamp is installed on the vehicle, the horizontal angle of geometric visibility of the front position lamp shall be 45° outwards to 45° inwards.

For M1 and N1 category vehicles applying this alternative, where the front position lamp is mounted below 750 mm (measured according to the provisions of paragraph 5.8.1.), the inward horizontal angle of 45° may be reduced to 20° under the H plane.
For M1 and N1 category vehicles applying this alternative, the vertical angle of geometric visibility of the front position lamp shall be 15° above and below the horizontal.

For M1 and N1 category vehicles applying this alternative, where the front position lamp is mounted below 750 mm (measured according to the provisions of paragraph 5.8.1.), the downward vertical angle of 15° may be reduced to 5°.
For M1 and N1 category vehicles applying this alternative, to be considered visible the front position lamp shall provide an unobstructed view of the apparent surface of at least 12.5 cm2.

For M1 and N1 category vehicles applying this alternative, the illuminating surface area of any retro-reflector that does not transmit light shall be excluded from the unobstructed apparent surface of the front position lamp.
A closed-circuit tell-tale for the front position lamps shall be mandatory.
The front position lamp tell-tale shall be non-flashing.
A tell-tale indicating failure of the front position lamps shall be mandatory if required by the component regulation.
Side-marker lamps shall be mandatory on all vehicles the length of which exceeds 6 m, except for chassis-cabs.
The SM1 type of side-marker lamp shall be used on all categories of vehicles, however the SM2 type of side-marker lamp may be used on M1 category vehicles.

On M1 and N1 category vehicles less than 6 m in length, side-marker lamps shall be used if they supplement the reduced geometric visibility requirements of front position lamps conforming to paragraph 6.9.5.2. and rear position lamps conforming to paragraph 6.10.5.2.
The minimum number of side-marker lamps per side shall be such that the rules for longitudinal positioning are complied with.
The side-marker lamps shall be type-approved according to the 00 or subsequent series of amendments to UN Regulation No. 91, or to the 00 or subsequent series of amendments to UN Regulation No. 148.
The side-marker lamps shall be positioned in height above the ground not less than 250 mm nor more than 1,500 mm (2,100 mm if the shape of the bodywork makes it impossible to keep within 1,500 mm).
At least one side-marker lamp shall be fitted to the middle third of the vehicle.
The foremost side-marker lamp shall be not further than 3 m (4 m for semi-trailers) from the front of the vehicle.
The distance between two adjacent side-marker lamps shall not exceed 3 m, or 4 m if the structure, design or the operational use of the vehicle makes it impossible to comply with 3 m.

For vehicles the length of which does not exceed 6 m and for chassis-cabs, it shall be sufficient to have one side-marker lamp fitted within the first third and/or within the last third of the vehicle length.

For M1 vehicles the length of which exceeds 6 m but does not exceed 7 m, it shall be sufficient to have one side-marker lamp fitted not further than 3 m from the front and one within the last third of the vehicle length.

The horizontal angle of geometric visibility of the side-marker lamps shall be 45° to the front and to the rear, except that for vehicles on which the installation of the side-marker lamps is optional this value can be reduced to 30°.

If the vehicle is equipped with side-marker lamps used to supplement the reduced geometric visibility of front and rear direction indicator lamps conforming to paragraph 6.5.5.2. and/or position lamps conforming to paragraphs 6.9.5.2. and 6.10.5.2., the horizontal angles of geometric visibility of these side-marker lamps shall be 45° towards the front and rear ends of the vehicle and 30° towards the centre of the vehicle.

The vertical angle of geometric visibility of the side-marker lamps shall be 10° above and below the horizontal, except that where a lamp is mounted below 750 mm (measured according to the provisions of paragraph 5.8.1.) the downward angle of 10° may be reduced to 5°.

Where amber side-marker lamps on M1 and N1 category vehicles less than 6 m in length are wired to flash, this flashing shall be in phase and at the same frequency with the direction-indicator lamps at the same side of the vehicle.
If a tell-tale for the side-marker lamps exists, its function shall be carried out by the tell-tale required for the front and rear position lamps.
A tell-tale indicating failure of the side-marker lamps shall be provided if required by the component regulation.

The distance in width between the inner edges of the apparent surfaces of the daytime running lamps in the direction of the reference axes shall not be less than 600 mm, except that this distance may be reduced to 400 mm where the overall width of the vehicle is less than 1,300 mm.
The daytime running lamps shall be positioned in height not less than 250 mm nor more than 1,500 mm above the ground.

The daytime running lamps shall be positioned in length at the front of the vehicle, this requirement being deemed satisfied if the light emitted does not cause discomfort to the driver either directly or indirectly through the devices for indirect vision and/or other reflecting surfaces of the vehicle.

The daytime running lamps shall be switched ON automatically when the device which starts and/or stops the propulsion system is set in a position which makes it possible for the propulsion system to operate and none of the following exist: (a) the front fog lamps are switched ON; (b) the headlamps are manually switched ON, except when they are used to give intermittent luminous warnings at short intervals; (c) conditions of Annex 13 for automatic switching ON of dipped-beam headlamps exist.

The automatic operation of the daytime running lamps shall be resumed as soon as the conditions described in paragraph 6.19.7.2. (automatic transmission control in park position, parking brake locked, prior to first motion after manual activation of the propulsion start/stop device, or vehicle speed not exceeding 15 km/h) no longer exist.

The daytime running lamp shall switch OFF automatically when the device which starts and/or stops the propulsion system is set in a position which makes it impossible for the propulsion system to operate.
The daytime running lamp shall switch OFF automatically when the front fog lamps are switched ON.
The daytime running lamp shall switch OFF automatically when the headlamps are manually switched ON, except when they are used to give intermittent luminous warnings at short intervals.
The daytime running lamp shall switch OFF automatically when the conditions of Annex 13 for automatic switching ON of dipped-beam headlamps exist.

If a front direction-indicator lamp is not reciprocally incorporated with a daytime running lamp and the distance between the edges of the apparent surfaces in the direction of the reference axis of the front direction-indicator lamp and the daytime running lamp is equal or less than 40 mm, the electrical connections of the daytime running lamp shall be such that either (a) the daytime running lamp on the relevant side of the vehicle is switched OFF during the entire period (both ON and OFF cycle) of operation of the front direction-indicator lamp, or (b) the luminous intensity of the daytime running lamp on the relevant side of the vehicle is reduced during the entire period (both ON and OFF cycle) of operation of the front direction-indicator lamp to attain not more than 140 cd within the angles of geometric visibility, unless the luminous intensity of the front direction-indicator lamp in HV is at least 50% higher than the luminous intensity of the daytime running lamp in HV.

If a front direction-indicator lamp is reciprocally incorporated with a daytime running lamp with totally common apparent surfaces, the electrical connections shall be such that the daytime running lamp function on the relevant side of the vehicle is switched OFF during the entire period (both ON and OFF cycle) of operation of the front direction-indicator lamp.

If a front direction-indicator lamp is reciprocally incorporated with a daytime running lamp with partially common apparent surfaces, the electrical connections of the daytime running lamp shall be such that either (a) the whole daytime running lamp function on the relevant side of the vehicle is switched OFF during the entire period (both ON and OFF cycle) of activation of the front direction-indicator lamp, or (b) for category 1a or 1b front direction-indicator lamp, the daytime running lamp function on the relevant side of the vehicle is switched OFF for the part of the apparent surface in common with that of the front direction-indicator lamp and the luminous intensity of the part of the apparent surface not in common is reduced during the entire period (both ON and OFF cycle) of operation of the front direction-indicator lamp to attain not more than 140 cd within the angles of geometric visibility.
The emergency stop signal shall be given by the simultaneous operation of all the stop or direction-indicator lamps fitted as described in paragraph 6.23.7.
All the lamps of the emergency stop signal shall flash in phase at a frequency of 4.0 ± 1.0 Hz.
The emergency stop signal shall operate independently of other lamps.

Where a rear-end collision alert signal is fitted (optional), the rear-end collision alert signal shall be given by the simultaneous operation of all the direction indicator lamps fitted, in accordance with the electrical connection requirements for the rear-end collision alert signal.
The position in width of the lamp used for the answer-back signal shall be in accordance with the individual specifications applicable to the specific lamp used for the answer-back signal.
The position in height of the lamp used for the answer-back signal shall be in accordance with the individual specifications applicable to the specific lamp used for the answer-back signal.
The position in length of the lamp used for the answer-back signal shall be in accordance with the individual specifications applicable to the specific lamp used for the answer-back signal.
The answer-back signal shall only operate under the park condition of a vehicle.
If the answer-back signal flashes, the frequency shall not exceed 2.0 Hz.

The answer-back signal shall be provided by approved lighting and light-signalling devices and exterior courtesy lamps where in all these cases the maximum luminous intensity per lamp does not exceed 700 cd on or above the HH line.
Front fog lamps, rear fog lamps and stop lamps shall not be used to provide the answer-back signal.

The duration of the optical indication of the answer-back signal, defined from the beginning to the end of the signal irrespective of whether it contains flashes, variations of intensity or variations in apparent surface, shall not exceed 3 seconds.

The position of lamps, as defined in paragraph 2.1.6., in width, in height and in length shall comply with the general requirements set out in paragraphs 2.10.2., 2.10.3., 2.10.4., 2.3.3. and 5.4., such that the measured distances fulfil the individual specifications applicable to each lamp.

The angles of geometric visibility of lamps, checked in accordance with paragraph 2.10.7., shall fulfil the individual specifications applicable to each lamp, except that the limits of the angles may have an allowance corresponding to the ±3° variation permitted in paragraph 5.3. for the mounting of the light-signalling devices.
The visibility of red light towards the front and of white light towards the rear shall comply with paragraph 5.10.

The lamps and tell-tales, with every lamp supplied by the electrical system of the vehicle switched on, shall function in accordance with the provisions set out in paragraphs 5.11. to 5.14. and with the individual specifications applicable to each lamp.

The presence, number, colour, arrangement and, where applicable, the category of lamps, as verified by visual inspection of the lamps and their markings, shall be such that the requirements set out in paragraphs 5.15. and 5.16. as well as in the individual specifications applicable to each lamp are fulfilled.

When tested in accordance with Annex 5, paragraph 1 (Flexible lower legform impactor), the absolute value of the maximum dynamic medial collateral ligament elongation at the knee shall not exceed 22 mm, the maximum dynamic anterior and posterior cruciate ligament elongation shall not exceed 13 mm, and the absolute value of dynamic bending moments at the tibia shall not exceed 340 Nm.

When tested in accordance with Annex 5, paragraph 2 (upper legform to bumper), the instantaneous sum of the impact forces with respect to time shall not exceed 7.5 kN and the bending moment on the test impactor shall not exceed 510 Nm, with the upper legform impactor certified pursuant to Annex 6, paragraph 2.

All devices designed to protect vulnerable road users when impacted by the vehicle shall be correctly activated before and/or be active during the relevant test, and it shall be the responsibility of the manufacturer to show that any devices will act as intended in a pedestrian impact.
For vehicles with a lower bumper height of less than 425 mm, the lower legform to bumper requirements of paragraph 4.1.1. shall be applied.
The HIC recorded shall not exceed 1,000 over two thirds of the combined child and adult headform test areas.
The HIC for the remaining areas shall not exceed 1,700 for both headforms.
In case there is only a child headform test area, the HIC recorded shall not exceed 1,000 over two thirds of the test area.
In case there is only a child headform test area, the HIC for the remaining area shall not exceed 1,700.
The HIC recorded shall not exceed 1,000 over a minimum of one half of the child headform test area.

In the flexible lower legform to bumper test, the direction of the impact velocity vector shall be in the horizontal plane and parallel to the longitudinal vertical plane of the vehicle with a tolerance of ± 2° in the horizontal and longitudinal plane at the time of first contact, and the axis of the impactor shall be perpendicular to the horizontal plane with a roll and pitch angle tolerance of ± 2° in the lateral and longitudinal plane.

In the flexible lower legform to bumper test, the bottom of the impactor (without parts needed for the purposes of launching and/or protection) shall be 75 mm above the ground reference plane at the time of the first contact with the bumper, with a tolerance of ± 10 mm.
